long_biography.plain_text:
Naval architect and marine engineer Simeon P. Palios entered shipping in 1969 and later founded Diana Shipping Agencies, where he remained managing director until the public-company era. From a Chios family with deep maritime experience, he combined inherited industry access with technical training at Durham University. He developed a shipowning and management platform and led Diana Shipping through its New York listing as chairman and chief executive. He transferred the chief executive role in 2021 but remains chairman and a director.

Diana Shipping's latest annual filing attributes to Palios beneficial ownership of 5.7% of its common stock through Taracan Investments and Limon Compania Financiera, including shares issuable through warrants. That disclosed interest is distinct from the listed company's vessels, investments, debt and other corporate assets. His family background supplied knowledge and connections, while his creation and long operation of the principal Diana business distinguish him from a passive heir.

uncertainties.detail: The authoritative owner record uses Symeon P. Palios, while Diana Shipping's English-language material and SEC filing use Simeon P. Palios. Greek sources use Συμεών Παληός and the informal Simos. The exact current role and career chronology show that these forms identify the same person; the owner record's display spelling is retained.

The owner record states 1 July 1941, while a Greek-language interview quotes Palios as saying he was born on 17 July 1941. Because the current company biography omits a birth date, 17 is retained only as a sub-threshold review candidate.

Palios came from a family with deep maritime roots and a father who had entered shipowning. Public records nevertheless identify Palios as founder of the core Diana operating platform and do not establish a transfer of the principal listed-company ownership asset, supporting an advantaged-start rather than inherited classification.

The latest annual report discloses a 5.7 percent beneficial common-stock interest through two entities, including warrant-linked shares. It does not make Palios the majority shareholder and does not convert Diana Shipping's corporate fleet, investments, debt or other assets into personal property.
No dedicated Forbes profile, exact personal LinkedIn, Instagram, Wikipedia page or personal website was verified. Only the official Diana Shipping board biography is proposed as a company website.
Politics, irrelevant private-family detail, allegations, legal matters, controversy and all vessel-specific research are excluded. Family background is included only to calibrate wealth origin.
